title: Microsoft 365 admin center: dedicated License Requests page for Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: The navigation paths, PowerShell control and administrator roles are supported. One statement needs narrowing: the briefing says no source describes existing behaviour changing, but the release notes explicitly describe centralizing requests previously found through multiple menus or notifications.

claims.claim: The roadmap introduces a dedicated Microsoft 365 admin center page for Microsoft 365 Copilot license requests submitted by users.
claims.quote: We are introducing a new dedicated License Requests page in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center to help admins more easily discover, review, and manage Microsoft 365 Copilot license requests submitted by users.

claims.claim: Global admins, license admins and user admins can manage Microsoft 365 Copilot license requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Global admins, license admins, and user admins can manage these requests seamlessly in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Page-specific permissions for the new License Requests page are not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" permissions roles page. Read release notes, About administrator roles, Copilot growth opportunities and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; the request roles are documented generally, but no new-page permission matrix is given.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk; Open questions
claims.claim: The new page's default state is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "on by default" enable disable tenant switch. Read roadmap, release notes, self-service purchase settings and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; none states the new page's default or that admins must enable it.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: A tenant switch that turns the new License Requests page on or off is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "on by default" enable disable tenant switch. Read release notes, Manage self-service purchases and trials, and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; the purchase policy is per product, not a new-page switch.

claims.claim: As of November 2026, Learn has no dedicated article explaining the new page beyond its release note.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "dedicated" "article" Copilot Microsoft 365 admin center. Read release notes and Configure Microsoft Copilot settings; search also returns Manage self-service license requests, which documents Billing > Licenses > Requests rather than the new page.

claims.where: What's changing; controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether the dedicated page replaces, retains or is the same as the Billing > Licenses > Requests tab.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "Requests tab" replace. Read release notes and Manage self-service license requests; the partner announcement links the older article but does not identify that tab as the new page or explain whether it is retained.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls row 2; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The documented self-service license request list is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > Requests.
claims.quote: In the admin center, select the Navigation menu, and then select Billing > Licenses. On the Licenses page, select the Requests tab.

claims.claim: An API for the documented self-service license request process is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "self-service license requests" Microsoft Graph API approve deny. Read Manage self-service license requests and search excerpts; approval instructions are portal steps, and returned Graph approval operations concern Intune elevation or Entra roles, not these requests.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls row 2
claims.claim: Tasks in the self-service license request article require at least User Administrator or License Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a User Administrator or a License Administrator to complete the tasks in this article.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance controls row 2
claims.claim: AOBO partners require Global Administrator for the self-service license request article's tasks.
claims.quote: If you're a partner who's an Admin On Behalf Of (AOBO) a customer, you must have a role that's set to Global Administrator to complete the tasks in this article.

claims.where: controls[1].governs and note; What's changing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The existing request article applies to self-service purchased products and services, including requests for blocked products.
claims.quote: The information in this article only applies to self-service purchased products and services. If you turn off self-service purchases in your organization, you can set up a self-service license request process

claims.claim: The November 2026 partner announcement says most organizations' Copilot Chat limit notifications include an upgrade option.
claims.quote: Upgrade options: In most organizations, the limit notification includes an option to upgrade.

claims.claim: Users can select that upgrade option to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot license from their admin.
claims.quote: Users can select it to request a Microsoft 365 Copilot license from their admin

claims.claim: The partner announcement says admins can approve or deny those upgrade requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: their admin, who can approve or deny requests in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft ties direct-purchase upgrade options to the organization's per-product self-service purchase setting.
claims.quote: If the organization allows users to buy licenses directly, users might also see an option to purchase a license. Admins can turn off direct purchases for each product.

claims.claim: The self-service control is at Settings > Org settings > Services > Self-service trials and purchases > product > Do not allow.
claims.quote: go to the Settings > Org settings page. On the Services tab ... select Self-service trials and purchases. ... select the product name. ... select Allow, Allow for trials only, or Do not allow.

claims.claim: MSCommerce supports Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled" to disable a product's self-service purchases and trials.
claims.quote: To disable the policy setting for a specific product, run the following command: Update-MSCommerceProductPolicy -PolicyId AllowSelfServicePurchase -ProductId <ProductID> -Value "Disabled"

claims.claim: The documented portal steps for allowing or blocking self-service purchases and trials require Global Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be a Global Administrator to do the following steps.

claims.claim: Changing MSCommerce product policies requires Global or Billing Administrator.
claims.quote: The Global or Billing Administrator role for your tenant to change the MSCommerce product policies.

claims.claim: AOBO partners require Global Administrator for the portal self-service setting.
claims.quote: Partners who are Admins On Behalf Of (AOBO) a customer must have a role that is set to Global Administrator to do the following steps.

claims.claim: AOBO partners require Global Administrator to manage self-service purchases via PowerShell.
claims.quote: Partners who are Admins On Behalf Of (AOBO) a customer must have a role that's set to Global Administrator in order to manage and disable self-service purchases in the Microsoft 365 admin center and via PowerShell.

claims.claim: The available self-service product list includes Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: | Microsoft Copilot | CFQ7TTC0MM8R | No |

claims.claim: Users trying to make a self-service purchase of a blocked product can submit a license request to the admin.
claims.quote: When a user tries to make a self-service purchase for a product that you blocked, they can submit a request for a license to you, the admin.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an entitlement or license requirement for the License Requests page itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" licensing price meter admin center; Microsoft 365 admin center license requirements administrator license access admin center. Read release notes, license options, request article and admin roles; none specifies a license for this page.

claims.claim: No price or meter is published for the License Requests page itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" licensing price meter admin center; "License Requests" "Copilot" "price" approval. Read release notes, license options and request article; they state no page-specific price or meter.

claims.claim: A cost specifically attached to approval on the new page is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "price" approval. Read release notes, license options, request article and Copilot growth opportunities; licensing and use of unused or additional licenses are described, but no charge specifically for this page's approval is stated.

claims.claim: The assignment procedure following approval on the new dedicated page is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" approve assign licenses purchase. Read release notes, request article and Copilot growth opportunities. Assignment of unused or additional licenses is described generally; detailed steps are for the older Requests tab, not the new page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The release note describes no agent or automated approval action.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "audit" "API"; read the complete dedicated-page release-note entry. It describes admins reviewing, filtering, approving or denying requests and bulk actions, without specifying agents or automated approval.

claims.claim: The release note names no new data access for users from this admin page.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "fields" details data. Read the complete dedicated-page release-note entry; it describes administrator request management and faster access to licenses, not a new user data-access permission.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the new page's displayed data beyond requests, user/date filtering and bulk actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" "fields" details data. Read release notes and self-service request article; detailed product/requester/date/status fields are stated for the older Requests tab, not expressly for the new dedicated page.

claims.claim: No source says existing behaviour changes.
claims.quote: Previously, admins had to locate license requests through multiple menus or notifications. This new page centralizes all Copilot license requests, improving visibility and management efficiency.
claims.fix: Remove only ', so no source says existing behaviour changes' from the first sentence of the second paragraph of Why it matters. Retain the statement that Microsoft has not stated the page's default or required admin action; the release note does describe changed request discovery.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified whether the dedicated admin page changes users' visible interface.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "dedicated" "article" Copilot Microsoft 365 admin center. Read release notes and November announcements; the page changes admin navigation, and Chat upgrade notifications are described separately, without attributing a user-interface change to this page.

claims.claim: The cited license options page does not explain whether its Microsoft Copilot name differs from the release note's Microsoft 365 Copilot for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "License Requests" "Copilot" licensing price meter admin center. Read License options for Microsoft Copilot and the dedicated-page release note; the license page does not discuss this feature or explain a feature-specific distinction between those names.
